## Verdict

missing

## Bearer

RaceRecordingRepository — app-wear/src/main/java/com/mgilli/app_wear/race/RaceRecordingRepositoryImpl.kt

## Trigger

startClock, markSegment, undoLastMark, stopRace, markSent and findInProgress — the repository's own methods, already called by the race controllers — observed

## Today

RaceRecordingRepositoryImpl holds every race it opens in an in-memory
LinkedHashMap, keyed by id, with an in-memory AtomicLong id counter.
startClock, markSegment, undoLastMark, stopRace and markSent all read
and write only that map — none calls RaceDao. findInProgress reads the
same in-memory map. The repository, the four race controllers and
ExerciseSessionManager are all singletons, so when the process dies
the map is empty on the next launch: findInProgress returns nothing to
the five places that ask it, and the race in progress is gone.

## Expected

startClock, markSegment, undoLastMark, stopRace and markSent each
write the race — its segments, and, on markSegment, any new
retainedFactors or rejectedCalibrations entry — to the database before
returning, using RaceDao.upsert (or RaceDao.update once the row
exists), so the current state of the race in progress is durable
after every one of those calls. findInProgress reads the database
instead of the in-memory map, so a race left in progress at process
death is found again at start-up, with its correct segment index,
durations, marks, currentSegmentOpenedAt and calibration lists.
observeRecorded/eraseRecorded/publishRecorded keep working the same
way once the source of the race rows is the database rather than the
map.

## Searched

RaceRecordingRepositoryImpl, RaceDao, findInProgress, LinkedHashMap, RaceEntity, upsert
